question.text: Which of these Cat III strategies is GENERALLY expected to have the LOWEST volatility (annualised standard deviation) in a well-constructed book?

explanation.text: The Logic: Market-neutral sleeves, by design (Beta ~ 0, long/short pairs), have lowest systematic vol. Typical annualised vol 4-8%. Directional strategies (long, short-bias) and leveraged global-macro run 12-25%. The Trap: Others have higher vol due to directional or leverage posture. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C same ranking. XXI-B PMS covers similar vol profiles. Manager's Pro-Tip: Investors equate 'low vol' with 'safe' — market-neutral can still have tail risk (crowded trade unwinds, e.g. Aug-2007 quant quake). Show investors 99% 1-month CVaR in addition to vol, to pre-empt surprise drawdowns.
